  Film Commission (21), BC Steamship Company (1975) (17), BC Housing (16), BC Railway Company
  1972-2003 (16), First Peoples' Cultural Council (14), Liquor Distribution Branch (13, and 39 more
  inferred), BC Pavilion Corporation (12), WLC Developments (12), Labour Relations Board (11), Open
  Learning Agency (10), Coal and Petroleum Control Board (9), Science Council of BC (23 inferred), the
  Homeowner Protection Office after June 2001 (9 inferred). The Workers' Compensation Review Board,
  Appeal Division and WCAT (61 together) and BC Cancer and BC Transplant before PHSA (42) are also
  unplaced. *Where:* orders in council assigning statutes, the Estimates' votes, annual reports.
  BC Archives authority pages for WCB, the Civil Service Commission and EHSC failed in round 2; try
  them first. *Hand back:* `responsible-*.json`.
remaining_records: Join root D1 ministry_transfer_clauses.json and original cabinet-assignment orders, including OIC 897/1999 s 23 (housing), s 25 (HPO), OIC 652/2010 ss 15–16 (Games/Film), OIC 596/2024 and OIC 377/2025. Preserve the printed Provincial Rental Housing Commission wording where the source uses it.
For WCB 1917–1973, inspect annual Workmen's Compensation Board reports, Labour departmental reports and the contemporaneous Workers Compensation Act administration/assignment provisions.
For PRHC from 1973 and EHSC from 1974, inspect annual-report organization charts, Estimates vote descriptions, original department transfer orders and share/administration agreements.
For the Civil/Public Service transition, retrieve the commencement order under Public Service Act SBC 1973 c 143 s 78. Opened OIC 3664/1973 merely transmits a bill and is not commencement.
Recover the three BC Archives authority texts listed in search_ledger.json; supplement rather than replace statutory and annual-report evidence.
findings: Nine bounded responsibility records are supplied in responsible-crowns.json. They are observations or a specifically dated transfer, not continuous histories for all unplaced body-years.

The Civil Service Act expressly assigns administration to the Provincial Secretary in the 1948 consolidation, s 7, and the 1960 consolidation, s 8. These observations have year precision; they do not establish a fabricated 1 January boundary.

LDB financial Note 1 states a transfer to Agriculture and Food effective 17 July 2025. Financial-note checkpoints also identify BCIB under Finance in 2021/22 and Infrastructure in 2025/26, BC Railway under Transportation and Transit in 2025/26, and PavCo through Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport.

The Museum 2025/26 note prints Tourism, Arts and Culture. Retain that source wording; root D1 OIC 596/2024 Appendix B item 423 supplies the normalized Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport portfolio. Do not mistake a shortened financial-note label for a different ministry.

EHSC legal establishment is 30 May 1974, from the original Act and contemporary default commencement rule; this solves a legal-start subquestion, not the requested complete ministry chronology. OIC 2305/1974 separately sets ambulance arrangements from 1 July 1974.
BC Archives authority pages for WCB, Civil Service Commission and EHSC were attempted directly and through both search engines but not recovered. These failures are documented.
remaining_gaps: The 54 PRHC, 57 WCB and 31 EHSC unplaced body-years are not all resolved. Most other early periods named in WANTED remain incomplete in this Crown package.

Employment Standards Tribunal Labour/Attorney General conflict, BC Games, BC Film Commission, Steamship Company, WLC Developments, Labour Relations Board, Coal and Petroleum Control Board, Science Council, HPO and earlier health agencies need their own dated responsibility evidence.

A current statutory reference to the responsible minister does not identify the historical ministry; a funding route, auditor addressee, tabling practice or reporting checkpoint cannot alone establish a continuous responsible-ministry interval.

Nine local responsibility observations/transfers; join root D1 orders for further evidence.

items.title: E2 (P1) Ownership, administration and control, typed.
items.request:
For each Crown corporation: who holds
  its shares (or that it has none), who appoints its board (statute and section), who administers
  it under agreement, and from when. Known so far, as events only: BCTFA owns BC Railway Company
  (2010) and TI Corp (2018); the B.C. Ferry Authority is the sole voting shareholder of BC Ferry
  Services, with the Province's preferred shares; BC Housing administers PRHC and has controlled it
  since 26 January 2024; BCSHS is a member of HEABC. Needs the line types in G1.
remaining_records: For each corporate entity, retrieve dated memorandum/articles, share register and transfer/subscription documents, and compare them to the statutory shareholder provisions.
Retrieve each employer association's constitution/bylaws and ministerial approvals under Public Sector Employers Act ss 7 and 9 for the specific year being drawn.
Retrieve the Museum Act s 6 prescribed-date regulation and historical Coastal Ferry Act ss 5,7 amendments before extending those appointment rows backward.
Join D1 statute-assignment orders only where an edge refers to a generic responsible minister; retain the relation type.
findings: 126 source-specific typed relationship rows cover 51 subjects, including shares, legal form, appointment, nomination, administration, membership, agency status, regulation and service populations.

The matrix gives governing statutory sections and qualifications. It distinguishes government ownership of the corporate share from pension-client assets, minister nomination from final appointment, accounting control from a documented share transfer, and corporate ownership from contractual administration.

WorkSafeBC president is appointed by the board, while WCAT chair is appointed by LGIC and its vice-chairs/extraordinary members by the chair after ministerial consultation. Employer associations have mixed government/member arrangements governed by approved bylaws.
R3E-R057–R060 use the statutory B.C. Ferry Authority name for the modern 2003 authority. The repository id bc-ferry-authority belongs to the 1964–1977 entity and must not be reused.
All typed rows explicitly decline to treat ownership, appointment, administration, funding or regulation alone as a complete accountability path to the people.
remaining_gaps: The matrix does not cover every Crown throughout every year. Most current statute observations have no proven historic start, and must not be backdated to incorporation.
Historic board-composition amendments, business-corporation articles/share registers, employer-association dated bylaws and some original administration agreements remain missing.
The Museum Act conditional nomination split needs the prescribed-date regulation. Ferry board composition changed, so today's four LGIC positions cannot be inserted into the original 2003 board.

findings: Coastal Ferry Act was assented to 27 March 2003 and expressly commenced 1 April 2003 under s 89. The modern B.C. Ferry Authority is established by s 2; the Commissioner's office by s 35.
The operator converted on 2 April 2003. Crown-agent cessation is Coastal Ferry Act s 19(3), correcting the earlier package's erroneous s 20(3) citation.

Audited company Note 8(b), PDF p. 57 / printed p. 55, records amendment of the memorandum and issue on 2 April 2003 of one voting Class B common share and 75,477 Class C preferred shares; the Authority holds common and the Province preferred. Preferred terms are $1,000 par and 8% cumulative.
Original Coastal Ferry Services Contract began 1 April 2003 with a sixty-year term. Four-year performance terms are not renewals of the whole agreement; PT 6 is 1 April 2024–31 March 2028.

All 18 published contract amendments are preserved in a ledger distinguishing reference, execution and effective dates. The modern authority needs a separate node from the repository's historical 1964–1977 Ferry Authority.

items.title: E5 (P2) Pensions and land titles.
items.request:
BCI and the BC Pension Corporation: corporate ownership
  apart from the pension boards and the assets they manage (Public Sector Pension Plans Act ss.
  5-8, 16-20). LTSA (2005): a non-share corporation, government agent only for specified purposes.
remaining_records: Retrieve 1999/2000 commencement orders for Public Sector Pension Plans Act corporate provisions and subsequent board amendments.
Retrieve LTSA establishment/commencement order for the 2005 transition and original operating agreement, then amendments affecting agency powers or ministerial administration.
Match historic nominations/appointments to the version of the statute then in force.
findings: Public Sector Pension Plans Act ss 5–8 establishes Pension Corporation ownership, agency status, administration and pension-board representation. Sections 16–20 separately establish BCI and its corporate share, board, investment-agent capacity and functions.
The government's corporate share does not make the pension/client funds ordinary assets of a ministry or imply pension boards own BCI shares.

LTSA is a non-profit non-share corporation; government-agent status is limited to Crown grants and agreement-defined purposes. Sections 6–7 distinguish stakeholder nomination and appointment by continuing directors; government nominates two positions.
LTSA s 41 exceptional ministerial administration under agreement is a separate mechanism from ordinary board appointment.
remaining_gaps: Original commencement instruments and changes in board composition have not all been traced. Current consolidated provisions are not complete dated historical intervals.
Original and amended LTSA operating agreements are needed to define its agency purposes for each period.
